text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The company organising next year's Commonwealth Games in Malaysia has been told its efforts so far have not been satisfactory and it would have to get moving on areas such as promotion and publicity by the Minister for Youth and Sports Muhyiddin Yassin

-- The youth wing of Malaysia's dominant United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) party has urged seven legislators under probe by the anti-corruption agency to go on leave. Malaysia has launched a massive anti-corruption drive initiated by Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

-- Malaysia is launching a nationwide monitoring for the Coxsackie B virus, that has killed 22 children in eastern Sarawak state in the last two months, by making it mandatory for all doctors to report cases, Health Minister Chua Jui Meng said.
-- The central Bank Negara Malaysia is yet to approve the start of negotiations for the merger between Suria Capital and MBf Capital

-- Malaysian Airline System Bhd has introduced ticketless travel. The national carrier's tickets can be booked at automated teller machines nationwide, a service launched by Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Tuesday.
